steps.check: R1 is a closed deg-5 triangular mesh (chi=2); subdivision keeps chi=2 and {5:12, 6:rest}
steps.determines: UNIQUE UP TO graph isomorphism (the icosahedron; its refinements are determined by it)
steps.expr: V=12,E=30,F=20,chi=2 all deg 5 (03's shell, re-derived cold); 1->4 subdivision keeps chi=2 and degree spectrum {5: the twelve, 6: the rest}
steps.what: the adjacency substrate: the icosahedron (closed deg-5 triangular mesh) and its combinatorial refinements R1..R4
steps.why: the observable needs a substrate to live on, and it must be the substrate's OWN adjacency, not an imported lattice. So the icosahedron is re-derived COLD: its twelve vertices (0,+-1,+-phi) & cyclic, edges = the pairs at the minimal squared distance (the pure integer 4 in Z[phi]; the other distances 4+4phi, 8+4phi are strictly larger, so the minimum is exact without any irrational comparison). The result satisfies container 03's OWN closed-mesh predicate -- triangular faces, every edge in two faces, uniform degree 5, Euler chi=2 -- so this re-exhibits the shell 03 SELECTED (via the three-observer separation), it does not merely trust it. The adjacency web is then REFINED by combinatorial 1->4 subdivision (an edge-midpoint registration, each triangle re-cut into four; pure combinatorics, no coordinates): a family R1..R4 of closed webs on the same 2-sphere bound, each with chi=2 and degree spectrum exactly {5: the original TWELVE, 6: every refinement vertex}. The twelve degree-5 sites persist at every level -- the seed Step 2's curvature concentrates on.

steps.check: on R1 every vertex has ball profile (1,6,11,12); pure adjacency, regional
steps.determines: UNIQUE (given the mesh and (v, r) the count is fixed)
steps.expr: |B_r(v)| = #{ registrations within r adjacency steps of v }; on R1 every vertex has profile (1, 6, 11, 12)
steps.what: the archic-density observable |B_r(v)|: a breadth-first count over adjacency
steps.why: ARCHIC DENSITY is the ball-growth observable: |B_r(v)| is the number of registrations within r adjacency STEPS of v -- a breadth-first count over the relation itself. It consults NO distance, NO embedding, NO angle; once A.1 fixes the edges, only adjacency is used. It is REGIONAL (a count over an r-neighbourhood, not a per-site number) -- which is what a density has to be. On R1 the mesh is vertex-transitive, so all twelve vertices share the identical profile (1, 6, 11, 12): the vertex, its 5 neighbours (|B_1|=6), its 5 second-neighbours (|B_2|=11), its antipode (|B_3|=12) -- the whole icosahedron by radius 3, its graph diameter.

steps.check: |B_1|=deg+1 (relabelling); R3: 2 degree classes < 4 ball-profile classes (deg-6 splits 3)
steps.determines: UNIQUE (the partition refinement is fixed by the meshes)
steps.expr: |B_1(v)| = deg(v)+1 (a relabelling at r=1, and the profile always determines the degree); on R3 degree gives 2 classes, ball growth gives 4 (150 deg-6 vertices split 60/30/60)
steps.what: finer than the degree, NOT a renaming: |B_1|=deg+1 but the profile strictly refines degree on R3
steps.why: the method demands a new observable prove it is not a relabelling of an old one. At r=1, |B_1(v)| = deg(v)+1 exactly -- so at r=1 ball growth IS the degree, and, generally, the profile always DETERMINES the degree (its r=1 entry), hence its partition of the vertices always REFINES the degree partition. The content is that it refines it STRICTLY: on R3 the degree sees only 2 classes (the twelve at 5, the 150 others at 6), while the ball profile sees 4 -- the 150 degree-6 vertices split into 3 profile classes (60/30/60). So two degree-6 vertices carry DIFFERENT ball profiles ((1,7,18,34) vs (1,7,19,35)) that the degree declares identical. A relabelling cannot separate what the degree identifies; ball growth does. It is a strictly finer observable -- and (foreshadowing Step 2 only) the class that grows slowest, (1,6,16,31), is exactly the twelve degree-5 sites: the observable already 'sees' where the curvature will sit.
